units.zh: 北齊書卷十一
units.en: Book of Northern Qi, Volume 11
units.literal: Book of Northern Qi, Volume 11

units.zh: 列傳第三
units.en: Biographies 3
units.literal: Biographies, Third

units.zh: 文襄六王
units.en: The Six Princes of Wenxiang
units.literal: The Six Princes of Wenxiang

units.zh: 河南康獻王孝瑜 廣寧王孝珩 河間王孝琬
units.en: Prince Kangxian of Henan (Xiaoyu); Prince of Guangning (Xiaoheng); Prince of Hejian (Xiaowan)
units.literal: Prince Kangxian of Henan, Xiaoyu; Prince of Guangning, Xiaoheng; Prince of Hejian, Xiaowan

units.zh: 蘭陵武王孝瓘 安德王延宗 漁陽王紹信
units.en: Prince Wu of Lanling (Xiaoguan); Prince of Ande (Yanzong); Prince of Yuyang (Shaoxin)
units.literal: Prince Wu of Lanling Xiaoguan; Prince of Ande Yanzong; Prince of Yuyang Shaoxin

units.zh: 文襄六男：文敬元皇后生河間王孝琬，宋氏生河南王孝瑜，王氏生廣寧王孝珩，蘭陵王長恭不得母氏姓，陳氏生安德王延宗，燕氏生漁陽王紹信。
units.en: Gao Cheng had six sons: Empress Yuan of Wenjing bore Prince Xiaowan of Hejian; Lady Song bore Prince Xiaoyu of Henan; Lady Wang bore Prince Xiaoheng of Guangning; Prince Changgong of Lanling never learned his mother's surname; Lady Chen bore Prince Yanzong of Ande; Lady Yan bore Prince Shaoxin of Yuyang.
units.literal: Wenxiang had six sons: Empress Yuan of Wenjing bore Prince Xiaowan of Hejian; Lady Song bore Prince Xiaoyu of Henan; Lady Wang bore Prince Xiaoheng of Guangning; Prince Changgong of Lanling’s mother’s surname could not be learned; Lady Chen bore Prince Yanzong of Ande; Lady Yan bore Prince Shaoxin of Yuyang.

units.zh: 河南康獻王孝瑜，字正德，文襄長子也。
units.en: Prince Xiaoyu of Henan, posthumously Prince Kangxian, style name Zhengde, was Wenxiang's eldest son.
units.literal: Prince Kangxian of Henan, Xiaoyu, style name Zhengde, was Wenxiang's eldest son.

units.zh: 初封河南郡公，齊受禪，進爵為王。
units.en: He was first made Duke of Henan Commandery. When Qi received the abdication, he was promoted to prince.
units.literal: He was first enfeoffed as Duke of Henan Commandery; when Qi received the abdication, his title was advanced to prince.

units.zh: 歷位中書令、司州牧。
units.en: He later served as Director of the Secretariat and Governor of Si Province.
units.literal: He successively held the posts of Director of the Secretariat and Governor of Si Province.

units.zh: 初，孝瑜養於神武宮中，與武成同年相愛。
units.en: Xiaoyu was initially raised in Shenwu's palace. He and Wucheng were the same age and were deeply attached to one another.
units.literal: At first Xiaoyu was raised in Shenwu's palace; he and Wucheng were the same age and loved each other.

units.zh: 將誅楊愔等，孝瑜預其謀。
units.en: When the plot was made to kill Yang Yin and the others, Xiaoyu was involved in it.
units.literal: When Yang Yin and the others were about to be executed, Xiaoyu took part in the plot.

units.zh: 及武成即位，禮遇特隆。
units.en: After Wucheng ascended the throne, he treated Xiaoyu with exceptional honor.
units.literal: When Wucheng came to the throne, the courtesy and treatment he gave Xiaoyu were especially generous.

units.zh: 帝在晉陽，手勑之曰：「吾飲汾清二盃，勸汝於鄴酌兩盃。」
units.en: While in Jinyang, the emperor sent him a handwritten edict: "I have drunk two cups of Fenqing; you should pour two cups in Ye as well."
units.literal: While the emperor was at Jinyang, he wrote him an edict in his own hand, saying, "I have drunk two cups of Fenqing; I urge you in Ye to pour two cups too."

units.zh: 其親愛如此。
units.en: Such was the affection between them.
units.literal: Their intimacy and affection were like this.

units.zh: 孝瑜容貌魁偉，精彩雄毅，謙慎寬厚，兼愛文學，讀書敏速，十行俱下，覆棋不失一道。
units.en: Xiaoyu was tall and imposing, with a bold, spirited bearing. Modest, cautious, and generous, he loved literature, read with exceptional speed, taking in ten lines at a glance, and when replaying a game never lost track of a single move.
units.literal: Xiaoyu's appearance was imposing and tall, his spirit bold and resolute; he was modest, cautious, generous, and also loved literature. He read swiftly, taking in ten lines at once, and when replaying a game never missed a single move.

units.zh: 初，文襄於鄴東起山池遊觀，時俗眩之。
units.en: When Wenxiang first built ornamental hills and pools for recreation east of Ye, the fashion dazzled the age.
units.literal: At first Wenxiang built hills, pools, and pleasure grounds east of Ye, and the fashion dazzled people at the time.

units.zh: 孝瑜遂於第作水堂、龍舟，植幡矟於舟上，數集諸弟宴射為樂。
units.en: Xiaoyu followed by building a water hall and dragon boat at his mansion, fitting the vessel with banners and spears and often gathering his brothers there for feasts and archery.
units.literal: Xiaoyu thereupon built a water hall and dragon boat at his residence, planted banners and spears on the boat, and several times gathered his younger brothers for feasting and archery as amusement.

units.zh: 武成幸其第，見而悅之，故盛興後園之玩，於是貴賤慕斅，處處營造。
units.en: When Wucheng visited Xiaoyu's mansion and liked what he saw, rear-garden amusements became all the rage. High and low alike rushed to imitate them, building such displays everywhere.
units.literal: Wucheng visited his residence, saw it, and was pleased by it; therefore amusements in rear gardens flourished greatly, and high and low alike emulated them, constructing them everywhere.

units.zh: 武成常使和士開與胡后對坐握槊，孝瑜諫曰：「皇后天下之母，不可與臣下接手。」
units.en: Gao Zhan often had He Shikai and Empress Hu sit facing each other playing shuo; Xiaoyu remonstrated, saying, "The empress is mother to all under Heaven — she must not touch hands with a subordinate minister."
units.literal: Wucheng often had He Shikai and Empress Hu sit facing each other playing shuo; Xiaoyu remonstrated, saying, "The empress is mother to all under Heaven — she must not touch hands with a subordinate minister."

units.zh: 帝深納之。
units.en: The emperor took this deeply to heart.
units.literal: The emperor took this deeply to heart.

units.zh: 後又言趙郡王父死非命，不可親。
units.en: Later he also said that the Prince of Zhao Commandery, whose father had died by violence, should not be kept close.
units.literal: Later he also said that the Prince of Zhao Commandery's father had died by violence and should not be kept close.

units.zh: 由是叡及士開皆側目。
units.en: On this account both Gao Rui and He Shikai looked askance at him.
units.literal: On this account both Rui and Shikai looked askance at him.

units.zh: 士開密告其奢僭，叡又言山東唯聞河南王，不聞有陛下。
units.en: He Shikai secretly reported his extravagance and presumption; Gao Rui also said that east of the mountains one heard only of the Prince of Henan, and never of the emperor.
units.literal: Shikai secretly reported his extravagance and presumption; Rui also said that east of the mountains one heard only of the Prince of Henan, and never of Your Majesty.

units.zh: 帝由是忌之。
units.en: The emperor on this account came to resent him.
units.literal: The emperor on this account came to resent him.

units.zh: 尒朱御女名摩女，本事太后，孝瑜先與之通，後因太子婚夜，孝瑜竊與之言。
units.en: An Erzhu palace woman named Monü had originally served the empress dowager; Xiaoyu had first had relations with her, and later, on the night of the crown prince's wedding, stole away to speak with her.
units.literal: An Erzhu palace woman named Monü had originally served the empress dowager; Xiaoyu had first had relations with her, and later, on the night of the crown prince's wedding, Xiaoyu stole away to speak with her.

units.zh: 武成大怒，頓飲其酒三十七盃。
units.en: Gao Zhan was greatly enraged and made him drink thirty-seven cups of wine in succession.
units.literal: Wucheng was greatly enraged and made him drink thirty-seven cups of wine in succession.

units.zh: 體至肥大，腰帶十圍。
units.en: His body was extremely corpulent, his waist ten arm-spans around.
units.literal: His body was extremely corpulent, his waistband ten arm-spans around.

units.zh: 使婁子彥載以出，酖之於車。
units.en: He had Lou Ziyan carry him out and poison him in the carriage.
units.literal: He had Lou Ziyan carry him out and poison him in the carriage.

units.zh: 至西華門，煩熱躁悶，投水而絕。
units.en: At the West Flowery Gate he grew feverish and stifled with distress, threw himself into the water, and died.
units.literal: At the West Flowery Gate he grew feverish and stifled with distress, threw himself into the water, and died.

units.zh: 贈太尉、錄尚書事。
units.en: He was posthumously appointed Grand Commandant and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
units.literal: He was posthumously appointed Grand Commandant and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 子弘節嗣。
units.en: His son Hongjie succeeded.
units.literal: His son Hongjie succeeded.

units.zh: 孝瑜母，魏吏部尚書宋弁孫也，本魏潁川王斌之妃，為文襄所納，生孝瑜，孝瑜還第，為太妃。
units.en: Xiaoyu's mother was a granddaughter of Song Bian, Wei's Minister of Personnel. She had originally been consort to Prince Bin of Yingchuan in Wei, but Wenxiang took her into his household and she bore Xiaoyu. When Xiaoyu took up residence in his own mansion, she became Grand Consort.
units.literal: Xiaoyu's mother was the granddaughter of Song Bian, Minister of Personnel under Wei. She had originally been the consort of Prince Bin of Yingchuan in Wei; Wenxiang took her into his household, and she bore Xiaoyu. When Xiaoyu returned to his residence, she became Grand Consort.

units.zh: 孝瑜妃，盧正山女，武成胡后之內姊也。
units.en: Xiaoyu's consort was a daughter of Lu Zhengshan and an elder sister of Emperor Wucheng's Empress Hu.
units.literal: Xiaoyu's consort was the daughter of Lu Zhengshan and was the elder sister of Wucheng's Empress Hu.

units.zh: 孝瑜薨後，宋太妃為盧妃所譖訴，武成殺之。
units.en: After Xiaoyu died, Consort Lu brought slanderous accusations against Grand Consort Song, and Wucheng had Song killed.
units.literal: After Xiaoyu died, Grand Consort Song was slanderously accused by Consort Lu, and Wucheng killed her.

units.zh: 廣寧王孝珩，文襄第二子也。
units.en: Prince Xiaoheng of Guangning was Gao Cheng's second son.
units.literal: Prince Xiaoheng of Guangning was Wenxiang's second son.

units.zh: 歷位司州牧、尚書令、司空、司徒、錄尚書、大將軍、大司馬。
units.en: He rose in succession to Governor of Si Province, Chief Minister of the Secretariat, Minister of Works, Minister over the Masses, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Grand General, and Grand Marshal.
units.literal: He rose in succession to Governor of Si Province, Chief Minister of the Secretariat, Minister of Works, Minister over the Masses, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Grand General, and Grand Marshal.

units.zh: 孝珩愛賞人物，學涉經史，好綴文，有伎藝。
units.en: Xiaoheng loved and appreciated men of talent; he studied the classics and histories, enjoyed composing literary pieces, and possessed artistic skill.
units.literal: Xiaoheng loved and appreciated men of talent; he studied the classics and histories, enjoyed composing literary pieces, and possessed artistic skill.

units.zh: 嘗於廳事壁自畫一蒼鷹，見者皆以為真，又作朝士圖，亦當時之妙絕。
units.en: Once on the wall of his reception hall he painted an azure hawk himself; viewers all took it for real. He also made a painting of court gentlemen — both were marvels of the age.
units.literal: Once on the wall of his reception hall he painted an azure hawk himself; viewers all took it for real; he also made a painting of court gentlemen — both were marvels of the age.

units.zh: 後主自晉州敗奔鄴，詔王公議於含光殿。
units.en: When the Last Emperor fled in defeat from Jinzhou to Ye, an edict summoned the princes and dukes to deliberate in the Hall of Contained Light.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor fled in defeat from Jinzhou to Ye, an edict summoned the princes and dukes to deliberate in the Hall of Contained Light.

units.zh: 孝珩以大敵既深，事藉機變。
units.en: Xiaoheng said that with the great enemy already pressing deep, affairs must rely on swift adaptation.
units.literal: Xiaoheng said that with the great enemy already pressing deep, affairs must rely on swift adaptation.

units.zh: 宜使任城王領幽州道兵入土門，揚聲趣并州；
units.en: The Prince of Rencheng should be sent to lead the Youzhou-route troops through Tumen Pass, proclaiming that he was marching on Bing Province;
units.literal: The Prince of Rencheng should be sent to lead the Youzhou-route troops through Tumen Pass, proclaiming that he was marching on Bing Province;

units.zh: 獨孤永業領洛州兵趣潼關，揚聲趣長安；
units.en: Dugu Yongye should lead the Luozhou troops toward Tong Pass, proclaiming that he was marching on Chang'an;
units.literal: Dugu Yongye should lead the Luozhou troops toward Tong Pass, proclaiming that he was marching on Chang'an;

units.zh: 臣請領京畿兵出滏口，鼓行逆戰。
units.en: your servant asks to lead the capital-region troops out through Fukou and advance with drums beating to meet the enemy.
units.literal: your servant asks to lead the capital-region troops out through Fukou and advance with drums beating to meet the enemy.

units.zh: 敵聞南北有兵，自然潰散。
units.en: When the enemy heard that there were armies north and south, they would naturally scatter in rout.
units.literal: When the enemy heard that there were armies north and south, they would naturally scatter in rout.

units.zh: 又請出宮人珍寶賜將士，帝不能用。
units.en: He also asked that palace women and precious objects be brought out to reward the officers and soldiers; the emperor would not adopt this.
units.literal: He also asked that palace women and precious objects be brought out to reward the officers and soldiers; the emperor would not adopt this.

units.zh: 承光即位，以孝珩為太宰。
units.en: When Chengguang succeeded to the throne, Xiaoheng was made Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: When Chengguang succeeded to the throne, Xiaoheng was made Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 與呼延族、莫多婁敬顯、尉相願同謀，期正月五日，孝珩於千秋門斬高阿那肱，相願在內以禁兵應之，族與敬顯自遊豫園勒兵出。
units.en: He joined with Huyan Zu, Moduolou Jingxian, and Wei Xiangyuan in a common plot, fixing the fifth day of the first month: Xiaoheng was to behead Gao Anaogong at the Gate of a Thousand Autumns; Xiangyuan inside would respond with the forbidden guard; Zu and Jingxian would lead troops out from the Pleasure Garden.
units.literal: He joined with Huyan Zu, Moduolou Jingxian, and Wei Xiangyuan in a common plot, fixing the fifth day of the first month: Xiaoheng was to behead Gao Anaogong at the Gate of a Thousand Autumns; Xiangyuan inside would respond with the forbidden guard; Zu and Jingxian would lead troops out from the Pleasure Garden.

units.zh: 既而阿那肱從別宅取便路入宮，事不果。
units.en: Before long Anaogong took a shortcut from another residence into the palace, and the affair did not succeed.
units.literal: Before long Anaogong took a shortcut from another residence into the palace, and the affair did not succeed.

units.zh: 乃求出拒西軍，謂阿那肱、韓長鸞、陳德信等云：「朝廷不賜遣擊賊，豈不畏孝珩反耶？
units.en: He then asked to go out to resist the western army, saying to Anaogong, Han Changluan, Chen Dexin, and the others, "The court will not grant permission to go out and strike the enemy — are you not afraid Xiaoheng will rebel?
units.literal: He then asked to go out to resist the western army, saying to Anaogong, Han Changluan, Chen Dexin, and the others, "The court will not grant permission to go out and strike the enemy — are you not afraid Xiaoheng will rebel?

units.zh: 孝珩破宇文邕，遂至長安，反時何與國家事。
units.en: If Xiaoheng defeats Yuwen Yong and then reaches Chang'an, what will rebellion have to do with the affairs of the state?
units.literal: If Xiaoheng defeats Yuwen Yong and then reaches Chang'an, what will rebellion have to do with the affairs of the state?

units.zh: 以今日之急，猶作如此猜疑。」
units.en: At today's urgent pass you still harbor such suspicions."
units.literal: At today's urgent pass you still harbor such suspicions."

units.zh: 高、韓恐其變，出孝珩為滄州刺史。
units.en: Gao and Han, fearing he might change, sent Xiaoheng out as Governor of Cang Province.
units.literal: Gao and Han, fearing he might change, sent Xiaoheng out as Governor of Cang Province.

units.zh: 至州，以五千人會任城王於信都，共為匡復計。
units.en: When he reached the province, he joined the Prince of Rencheng at Xindu with five thousand men to plan together for restoration.
units.literal: When he reached the province, he joined the Prince of Rencheng at Xindu with five thousand men to plan together for restoration.

units.zh: 周齊王憲來伐，兵弱不能敵。
units.en: Prince Xian of Zhou came to attack; their forces were weak and could not resist.
units.literal: Prince Xian of Zhou came to attack; their forces were weak and could not resist.

units.zh: 怒曰：「由高阿那肱小人，吾道窮矣！」
units.en: In anger he said, "Because of the petty man Gao Anaogong, my road is at an end!"
units.literal: In anger he said, "Because of the petty man Gao Anaogong, my road is at an end!"

units.zh: 齊叛臣乞扶令和以矟刺孝珩墜馬，奴白澤以身扞之，孝珩猶傷數處，遂見虜。
units.en: A Qi turncoat, Qifu Linghe, stabbed Xiaoheng with a spear and knocked him from his horse; the slave Baize shielded him with his body; Xiaoheng still suffered wounds in several places and was then taken captive.
units.literal: A Qi turncoat, Qifu Linghe, stabbed Xiaoheng with a spear and knocked him from his horse; the slave Baize shielded him with his body; Xiaoheng still suffered wounds in several places and was then taken captive.

units.zh: 齊王憲問孝珩齊亡所由，孝珩自陳國難，辭淚俱下，俯仰有節。
units.en: Prince Xian of Zhou asked Xiaoheng the reason for Qi's fall; Xiaoheng himself explained the state's calamity, words and tears together falling, his bearing composed in every movement.
units.literal: Prince Xian of Zhou asked Xiaoheng the reason for Qi's fall; Xiaoheng himself explained the state's calamity, words and tears together falling, his bearing composed in every movement.

units.zh: 憲為之改容，親為洗創傅藥，禮遇甚厚。
units.en: Xian changed countenance on his account, personally washed his wounds and applied medicine, and treated him with great courtesy.
units.literal: Xian changed countenance on his account, personally washed his wounds and applied medicine, and treated him with great courtesy.

units.zh: 孝珩獨歎曰：「李穆叔言齊氏二十八年，今果然矣。
units.en: Xiaoheng sighed alone and said, "Li Mushu said the Qi house would last twenty-eight years — today it has indeed come to pass.
units.literal: Xiaoheng sighed alone and said, "Li Mushu said the Qi house would last twenty-eight years — today it has indeed come to pass.

units.zh: 自神武皇帝以外，吾諸父兄弟無一人得至四十者，命也。
units.en: Apart from Gao Huan, not one of my fathers and brothers among the clan reached forty — such is fate.
units.literal: Apart from the Shenwu Emperor, not one of my fathers and brothers among the clan reached forty — such is fate.

units.zh: 嗣君無獨見之明，宰相非柱石之寄，恨不得握兵符，受廟算，展我心力耳。」
units.en: The succeeding ruler lacked independent insight; the chief ministers were no pillars to rely upon — I only regret that I could not grasp the tally of command, receive the plans of the temple, and give full play to the strength of my heart."
units.literal: The succeeding ruler lacked independent insight; the chief ministers were no pillars to rely upon — I only regret that I could not grasp the tally of command, receive the plans of the temple, and give full play to the strength of my heart."

units.zh: 至長安，依例授開府、縣侯。
units.en: When he reached Chang'an, by precedent he was appointed Opener of an Office (kaifu) and Marquis of a county.
units.literal: When he reached Chang'an, by precedent he was appointed Opener of an Office (kaifu) and Marquis of a county.

units.zh: 後周武帝在雲陽，宴齊君臣，自彈胡琵琶，命孝珩吹笛。
units.en: Later, when Emperor Wu of Zhou was at Yunyang, he feasted the Qi ruler and ministers, himself playing the barbarian pipa and ordering Xiaoheng to play the flute.
units.literal: Later, when Emperor Wu of Zhou was at Yunyang, he feasted the Qi ruler and ministers, himself playing the barbarian pipa and ordering Xiaoheng to play the flute.

units.zh: 辭曰：「亡國之音，不足聽也。」
units.en: He declined, saying, "The music of a fallen state is not worth hearing."
units.literal: He declined, saying, "The music of a fallen state is not worth hearing."

units.zh: 固命之，舉笛裁至口，淚下嗚咽，武帝乃止。
units.en: Though pressed he obeyed; he raised the flute barely to his lips, tears falling in sobs, and Emperor Wu then stopped.
units.literal: Though pressed he obeyed; he raised the flute barely to his lips, tears falling in sobs, and Emperor Wu then stopped.

units.zh: 其年十月，疾甚，啟歸葬山東，從之。
units.en: In the tenth month of that year his illness grew severe; he petitioned to be buried back in Shandong, and permission was granted.
units.literal: In the tenth month of that year his illness grew severe; he petitioned to be buried back in Shandong, and permission was granted.

units.zh: 尋卒，令還葬鄴。
units.en: Before long he died; an order was issued to return his body for burial at Ye.
units.literal: Before long he died; an order was issued to return his body for burial at Ye.

units.zh: 孝琬以文襄世嫡，驕矜自負。
units.en: Xiaowan, as Gao Cheng's legitimate heir of the generation, was proud and self-important.
units.literal: Xiaowan, as Wenxiang's legitimate heir of the generation, was proud and self-important.

units.zh: 河南王之死，諸王在宮內莫敢舉聲，唯孝琬大哭而出。
units.en: At Prince Xiaoyu of Henan's death, the princes within the palace did not dare raise a sound; only Xiaowan wept loudly and went out.
units.literal: At the Prince of Henan's death, the princes within the palace did not dare raise a sound; only Xiaowan wept loudly and went out.

units.zh: 又怨執政，為草人而射之。
units.en: He also resented those in power and made a straw effigy which he shot at.
units.literal: He also resented those in power and made a straw effigy which he shot at.

units.zh: 和士開與祖珽譖之，云：「草人擬聖躬也。
units.en: He Shikai and Zu Ting slandered him, saying, "The straw effigy was modeled on the sacred person.
units.literal: He Shikai and Zu Ting slandered him, saying, "The straw effigy was modeled on the sacred person.

units.zh: 又前突厥至州，孝琬脫兜鍪抵地，云『豈是老嫗，須著此』。
units.en: Moreover, when the Turks earlier came to the province, Xiaowan took off his helmet and cast it to the ground, saying, 'Am I an old woman that I must wear this?'
units.literal: Moreover, when the Turks earlier came to the province, Xiaowan took off his helmet and cast it to the ground, saying, 'Am I an old woman that I must wear this?'

units.zh: 此言屬大家也。」
units.en: These words were directed at Your Majesty."
units.literal: These words were directed at Your Majesty."

units.zh: 初，魏世謠言：「河南種穀河北生，白楊樹頭金雞鳴。」
units.en: Earlier, in Wei times there was a rhyme: "Henan plants grain, Hebei gives birth; on the white poplar's crown a golden cock crows."
units.literal: Earlier, in Wei times there was a rhyme: "Henan plants grain, Hebei gives birth; on the white poplar's crown a golden cock crows."

units.zh: 珽以說曰：「河南、河北，河間也。
units.en: Ting used this to explain, saying, "Henan and Hebei mean Hejian.
units.literal: Ting used this to explain, saying, "Henan and Hebei mean Hejian.

units.zh: 金雞鳴，孝琬將建金雞而大赦。」
units.en: The golden cock's crow means Xiaowan will build a golden cock and proclaim a great amnesty."
units.literal: The golden cock's crow means Xiaowan will build a golden cock and proclaim a great amnesty."

units.zh: 帝頗惑之。
units.en: The emperor was quite swayed.
units.literal: The emperor was quite swayed.

units.zh: 時孝琬得佛牙，置於第內，夜有神光。
units.en: At the time Xiaowan had obtained a Buddha tooth and placed it in his residence; at night there was divine light.
units.literal: At the time Xiaowan had obtained a Buddha tooth and placed it in his residence; at night there was divine light.

units.zh: 昭玄都法順請以奏聞，不從。
units.en: Fashun of Zhaoxuan Abbey asked to report it to the throne; he would not consent.
units.literal: Fashun of Zhaoxuan Abbey asked to report it to the throne; he would not consent.

units.zh: 帝聞，使搜之，得鎮庫矟幡數百。
units.en: When the emperor heard of it, he sent men to search the residence and found several hundred spears and banners from the arsenal.
units.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he sent men to search the residence and found several hundred spears and banners from the arsenal.

units.zh: 帝聞之，以為反。
units.en: When the emperor heard of this, he took it for rebellion.
units.literal: When the emperor heard of this, he took it for rebellion.

units.zh: 訊其諸姬，有陳氏者無寵，誣對曰「孝琬畫作陛下形哭之」，然實是文襄像，孝琬時時對之泣。
units.en: His concubines were interrogated; one surnamed Chen, who had no favor, falsely answered that "Xiaowan painted the emperor's likeness and wept before it" — but in truth it was a portrait of Gao Cheng, before which Xiaowan often wept.
units.literal: His concubines were interrogated; one surnamed Chen, who had no favor, falsely answered that "Xiaowan painted the emperor's likeness and wept before it" — but in truth it was a portrait of Wenxiang, before which Xiaowan often wept.

units.zh: 帝怒，使武纫赫連輔玄倒鞭撾之。
units.en: The emperor was enraged and ordered the guard Helian Fuxuan to beat him with an inverted whip.
units.literal: The emperor was enraged and ordered the guard Helian Fuxuan to beat him with an inverted whip.

units.zh: 孝琬呼阿叔，帝怒曰：「誰是爾叔？
units.en: Xiaowan cried out "Uncle!" The emperor in anger said, "Who is your uncle?
units.literal: Xiaowan cried out "Uncle!" The emperor in anger said, "Who is your uncle?

units.zh: 敢喚我作叔！」
units.en: You dare call me uncle!"
units.literal: You dare call me uncle!"

units.zh: 孝琬曰：「神武皇帝嫡孫，文襄皇帝嫡子，魏孝靜皇帝外甥，何為不得喚作叔也？」
units.en: Xiaowan said, "Grandson of Gao Huan, son of Gao Cheng, nephew of Emperor Xiaojing of Wei — why may I not call you uncle?"
units.literal: Xiaowan said, "Grandson of Emperor Shenwu, son of Emperor Wenxiang, nephew of Emperor Xiaojing of Wei — why may I not call you uncle?"

units.zh: 帝愈怒，折其兩脛而死。
units.en: The emperor grew still more enraged and broke both his shins, and he died.
units.literal: The emperor grew still more enraged and broke both his shins, and he died.

units.zh: 瘞諸西山，帝崩後，乃改葬。
units.en: He was buried on the western hills; after the emperor's death he was reinterred.
units.literal: He was buried on the western hills; after the emperor's death he was reinterred.

units.zh: 子正禮嗣，幼聰穎，能誦左氏春秋。
units.en: His son Zhengli succeeded; in youth he was clever and sharp, and could recite the Zuo Tradition.
units.literal: His son Zhengli succeeded; in youth he was clever and sharp, and could recite the Zuo Tradition.

units.zh: 齊亡，遷綿州卒。
units.en: When Qi fell he was transferred to Mian Prefecture, where he died.
units.literal: When Qi fell he was transferred to Mian Prefecture, where he died.

units.zh: 蘭陵武王長恭，一名孝瓘，文襄第四子也。
units.en: Prince Wu of Lanling, Changgong — also named Xiaoguan — was Gao Cheng's fourth son.
units.literal: Prince Wu of Lanling, Changgong — also named Xiaoguan — was Wenxiang's fourth son.

units.zh: 累遷并州刺史。
units.en: He was promoted in succession to Governor of Bing Province.
units.literal: He was promoted in succession to Governor of Bing Province.

units.zh: 突厥入晉陽，長恭盡力擊之。
units.en: When the Turks entered Jinyang, Changgong exerted himself to the utmost in striking them.
units.literal: When the Turks entered Jinyang, Changgong exerted himself to the utmost in striking them.

units.zh: 芒山之敗，長恭為中軍，率五百騎再入周軍，遂至金墉之下，被圍甚急，城上人弗識，長恭免冑示之面，乃下弩手救之，於是大捷。
units.en: At the defeat at Mang Mountain, Changgong served as central army commander; leading five hundred horsemen he entered the Zhou army a second time and reached beneath the walls of Jinyong; besieged in extreme peril, those on the walls did not recognize him; Changgong removed his helmet to show his face, and only then did they lower crossbowmen to rescue him — whereupon there was a great victory.
units.literal: At the defeat at Mang Mountain, Changgong served as central army commander; leading five hundred horsemen he entered the Zhou army a second time and reached beneath the walls of Jinyong; besieged in extreme peril, those on the walls did not recognize him; Changgong removed his helmet to show his face, and only then did they lower crossbowmen to rescue him — whereupon there was a great victory.

units.zh: 武士共歌謠之，為蘭陵王入陣曲是也。
units.en: The warriors together sang ballads of it — this is the Entry of the Prince of Lanling into Battle.
units.literal: The warriors together sang ballads of it — this is the Entry of the Prince of Lanling into Battle.

units.zh: 歷司州牧、青瀛二州，頗受財貨。
units.en: He served in succession as Governor of Si Province and of Qing and Ying provinces, and rather accepted goods and wealth.
units.literal: He served in succession as Governor of Si Province and of Qing and Ying provinces, and rather accepted goods and wealth.

units.zh: 後為太尉，與段韶討栢谷，又攻定陽。
units.en: Later he became Grand Commandant; with Duan Shao he attacked Baigu, and again attacked Dingyang.
units.literal: Later he became Grand Commandant; with Duan Shao he attacked Baigu, and again attacked Dingyang.

units.zh: 韶病，長恭總其衆。
units.en: Shao fell ill; Changgong took overall command of his forces.
units.literal: Shao fell ill; Changgong took overall command of his forces.

units.zh: 前後以戰功別封鉅鹿、長樂、樂平、高陽等郡公。
units.en: Before and after, for military merit he was separately enfeoffed Duke of Julu, Changle, Leping, Gaoyang, and other commanderies.
units.literal: Before and after, for military merit he was separately enfeoffed Duke of Julu, Changle, Leping, Gaoyang, and other commanderies.

units.zh: 芒山之捷，後主謂長恭曰：「入陣太深，失利悔無所及。」
units.en: After the victory at Mang Mountain, the Last Emperor said to Changgong, "You entered the battle line too deeply; if it had gone badly, regret would have availed nothing."
units.literal: After the victory at Mang Mountain, the Last Emperor said to Changgong, "You entered the battle line too deeply; if it had gone badly, regret would have availed nothing."

units.zh: 對曰：「家事親切，不覺遂然。」
units.en: He replied, "Family affairs touch one closely — without noticing it, I did so."
units.literal: He replied, "Family affairs touch one closely — without noticing it, I did so."

units.zh: 帝嫌其稱家事，遂忌之。
units.en: The emperor resented his speaking of family affairs and on this account came to be wary of him.
units.literal: The emperor resented his speaking of family affairs and on this account came to be wary of him.

units.zh: 及在定陽，其屬尉相願謂曰：「王既受朝寄，何得如此貪殘？」
units.en: When he was at Dingyang, his subordinate Wei Xiangyuan said to him, "Your Highness has received the court's commission — how can you be so greedy and cruel?"
units.literal: When he was at Dingyang, his subordinate Wei Xiangyuan said to him, "Your Highness has received the court's commission — how can you be so greedy and cruel?"

units.zh: 長恭未答。
units.en: Changgong did not reply.
units.literal: Changgong did not reply.

units.zh: 相願曰：「豈不由芒山大捷，恐以威武見忌，欲自穢乎？」
units.en: Xiangyuan said, "Is it not because of the great victory at Mang Mountain — fearing that your martial prestige would excite jealousy, and wishing to defile yourself?"
units.literal: Xiangyuan said, "Is it not because of the great victory at Mang Mountain — fearing that your martial prestige would excite jealousy, and wishing to defile yourself?"

units.zh: 長恭曰：「然。」
units.en: Changgong said, "It is so."
units.literal: Changgong said, "It is so."

units.zh: 相願曰：「朝廷若忌王，於此犯便當行罰，求福反以速禍。」
units.en: Xiangyuan said, "If the court resents Your Highness, for this offense it ought at once to punish you — seeking fortune instead hastens disaster."
units.literal: Xiangyuan said, "If the court resents Your Highness, for this offense it ought at once to punish you — seeking fortune instead hastens disaster."

units.zh: 長恭泣下，前膝請以安身術。
units.en: Changgong wept; going forward on his knees he asked for a method to preserve himself.
units.literal: Changgong wept; going forward on his knees he asked for a method to preserve himself.

units.zh: 相願曰：「王前既有勳，今復告捷，威聲太重，宜屬疾在家，勿預事。」
units.en: Xiangyuan said, "Your Highness already had merit before; now you report victory again — your martial renown is too heavy; you ought to plead illness and remain at home, and not take part in affairs."
units.literal: Xiangyuan said, "Your Highness already had merit before; now you report victory again — your martial renown is too heavy; you ought to plead illness and remain at home, and not take part in affairs."

units.zh: 長恭然其言，未能退。
units.en: Changgong agreed with his words but could not withdraw.
units.literal: Changgong agreed with his words but could not withdraw.

units.zh: 及江淮寇擾，恐復為將，歎曰：「我去年面腫，今何不發。」
units.en: When bandits harried the Jiang-Huai region, fearing he would again be made a general, he sighed and said, "Last year my face swelled — why does it not break out now?"
units.literal: When bandits harried the Jiang-Huai region, fearing he would again be made a general, he sighed and said, "Last year my face swelled — why does it not break out now?"

units.zh: 自是有疾不療。
units.en: From then on he had an illness and would not treat it.
units.literal: From then on he had an illness and would not treat it.

units.zh: 武平四年五月，帝使徐之範飲以毒藥。
units.en: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Wuping, the emperor had Xu Zhifan make him drink poison.
units.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Wuping, the emperor had Xu Zhifan make him drink poison.

units.zh: 長恭謂妃鄭氏曰：「我忠以事上，何辜於天，而遭鴆也。」
units.en: Changgong said to his consort Lady Zheng, "I served the ruler with loyalty — what crime have I against Heaven, that I should meet poison?"
units.literal: Changgong said to his consort Lady Zheng, "I served the ruler with loyalty — what crime have I against Heaven, that I should meet poison?"

units.zh: 妃曰：「何不求見天顏。」
units.en: The consort said, "Why do you not ask to see the imperial countenance?"
units.literal: The consort said, "Why do you not ask to see the imperial countenance?"

units.zh: 長恭曰：「天顏何由可見。」
units.en: Changgong said, "How could I ever look upon the emperor's face?"
units.literal: Changgong said, "How could the emperor's face ever be seen?"

units.zh: 遂飲藥薨。
units.en: He drank the poison and died.
units.literal: He then drank the poison and died.

units.zh: 贈太尉。
units.en: Posthumously he was made grand commandant.
units.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Commandant.

units.zh: 長恭貌柔心壯，音容兼美。
units.en: Changgong looked gentle but his heart was bold; in voice and bearing alike he was beautiful.
units.literal: Changgong's face was gentle but his heart was bold; voice and bearing alike were beautiful.

units.zh: 為將躬勤細事，每得甘美，雖一瓜數果，必與將士共之。
units.en: As a general he personally saw to the smallest things; whenever he had anything sweet or fine — even a melon or a few fruits — he shared it with his officers and men.
units.literal: As a general he personally attended to the smallest matters; whenever he obtained anything sweet or fine, even a single melon or a few fruits, he always shared them with his officers and men.

units.zh: 初在瀛州，行參軍陽士深表列其贓，免官。
units.en: While governor of Ying Province, the acting adjutant Yang Shishen submitted a detailed list of his corruption, and he was dismissed.
units.literal: At first, while in Ying Province, the acting adjutant Yang Shishen submitted a detailed list of his corrupt acts, and he was dismissed from office.

units.zh: 及討定陽，士深在軍，恐禍及。
units.en: During the campaign against Dingyang, Shishen was with the army and feared retribution.
units.literal: When they campaigned against Dingyang, Shishen was with the army, fearing that retribution would reach him.

units.zh: 長恭聞之曰：「吾本無此意。」
units.en: Changgong heard and said, "That was never my intent."
units.literal: Changgong heard of it and said, "I never had such an intention."

units.zh: 乃求小失，杖士深二十以安之。
units.en: He then found a minor fault, had Shishen beaten twenty strokes, and put the matter to rest.
units.literal: He then found a minor fault, had Shishen beaten twenty strokes, and so reassured him.

units.zh: 嘗入朝而僕從盡散，唯有一人，長恭獨還，無所譴罰。
units.en: Once on his way to court his attendants all fled save one; Changgong returned alone and punished no one.
units.literal: Once when he went to court his attendants all scattered, and only one remained; Changgong returned alone without punishing anyone.

units.zh: 武成賞其功，命賈護為買妾二十人，唯受其一。
units.en: Gao Zhan rewarded his service and ordered Jia Hu to buy him twenty concubines; he accepted only one.
units.literal: Wucheng rewarded his achievements and ordered Jia Hu to buy twenty concubines for him; he accepted only one.

units.zh: 有千金責券，臨死日，盡燔之。
units.en: He held promissory notes worth a thousand gold; on the day of his death he burned them all.
units.literal: He held promissory notes worth a thousand gold; on the day he died, he burned them all.

units.zh: 安德王延宗，文襄第五子也。
units.en: Prince Yanzong of Ande was the fifth son of Gao Cheng.
units.literal: Prince Yanzong of Ande was the fifth son of Wenxiang.

units.zh: 母陳氏，廣陽王妓也。
units.en: His mother was Lady Chen, a courtesan of the Prince of Guangyang.
units.literal: His mother was Lady Chen, a courtesan of the Prince of Guangyang.

units.zh: 延宗幼為文宣所養，年十二，猶騎置腹上，令溺己臍中，抱之曰：「可憐止有此一箇。」
units.en: Yanzong was raised from childhood by Gao Yang; even at twelve the emperor would set him astride his belly, make him urinate into his navel, hold him close and say, "Poor child — I have only this one."
units.literal: Yanzong was raised from childhood by Wenxuan; even at twelve Wenxuan would set him astride his belly, make him urinate into his navel, hold him close and say, "Pitiful — I have only this one."

units.zh: 問欲作何王，對曰：「欲作衝天王。」
units.en: He asked what title the boy wanted; Yanzong answered, "I want to be Prince Heaven-Storm."
units.literal: He asked what prince Yanzong wished to be; the boy answered, "I wish to be Prince Storm-the-Heavens."

units.zh: 文宣問楊愔，愔曰：「天下無此郡名，願使安於德。」
units.en: Gao Yang asked Yang Yin; Yang said, "No such commandery exists in the realm — let him dwell secure in virtue instead."
units.literal: Wenxuan asked Yang Yin; Yang said, "There is no such commandery in the realm — I wish he may dwell secure in virtue."

units.zh: 於是封安德焉。
units.en: And so he was enfeoffed Prince of Ande.
units.literal: And so he was enfeoffed as Prince of Ande.

units.zh: 為定州刺史，於樓上大便，使人在下張口承之。
units.en: As governor of Ding Province he would defecate from an upper story while men below opened their mouths to receive it.
units.literal: As governor of Ding Province, he would defecate from an upper story, having men below open their mouths to catch it.

units.zh: 以蒸嚢糝和人糞以飼左右，有難色者鞭之。
units.en: He mixed steamed grain with human dung to feed his attendants and whipped any who looked disgusted.
units.literal: He mixed steamed grain with human dung to feed his attendants, and whipped any who showed revulsion.

units.zh: 孝昭帝聞之，使趙道德就州杖之一百。
units.en: Emperor Gao Yan heard and sent Zhao Daode to the province to beat him a hundred strokes.
units.literal: Emperor Xiaozhao heard of it and sent Zhao Daode to the province to beat him a hundred strokes.

units.zh: 道德以延宗受杖不謹，又加三十。
units.en: Daode, finding Yanzong insufficiently deferential under the rod, added thirty strokes.
units.literal: Daode, seeing that Yanzong did not take the beating with proper deference, added thirty more.

units.zh: 又以囚試刀，驗其利鈍。
units.en: He also tested blades on prisoners to see whether they were sharp or dull.
units.literal: He also tested blades on prisoners to see whether they were sharp or dull.

units.zh: 驕縱多不法。
units.en: Arrogant and unrestrained, he broke the law in many ways.
units.literal: Arrogant and unrestrained, he committed many unlawful acts.

units.zh: 武成使撻之，殺其昵近九人，從是深自改悔。
units.en: Gao Zhan had him flogged and killed nine of his closest intimates; from that Yanzong deeply repented.
units.literal: Wucheng had him flogged and killed nine of his closest intimates; from this Yanzong deeply repented.

units.zh: 蘭陵王芒山凱捷，自陳兵勢，諸兄弟咸壯之。
units.en: When Prince Changgong of Lanling reported his victory at Mangshan and described his forces, all his brothers praised him.
units.literal: When Prince Changgong of Lanling reported his victory at Mangshan and described his military strength, all the brothers praised him.

units.zh: 延宗獨曰：「四兄非大丈夫，何不乘勝徑入？
units.en: Yanzong alone said, "Fourth brother is no true man — why not press the victory and march straight in?
units.literal: Yanzong alone said, "Fourth brother is no true man — why did he not press the advantage and march straight in?

units.zh: 使延宗當此勢，關西豈得復存。」
units.en: Had Yanzong held that position, how could the lands west of the passes still stand?"
units.literal: If Yanzong were in that position, how could the lands west of the passes still stand?"

units.zh: 及蘭陵死，妃鄭氏以頸珠施佛。
units.en: When Changgong of Lanling died, his consort Lady Zheng offered her neck-pearl to the Buddha.
units.literal: When Changgong of Lanling died, his consort Lady Zheng offered her neck-pearl to the Buddha.

units.zh: 廣寧王使贖之。
units.en: The Prince of Guangning sent men to redeem it.
units.literal: The Prince of Guangning sent men to redeem it.

units.zh: 延宗手書以諫，而淚滿紙。
units.en: Yanzong wrote a letter of remonstrance by hand, the page soaked with tears.
units.literal: Yanzong wrote a letter of remonstrance by hand, tears flooding the page.

units.zh: 河間死，延宗哭之淚亦甚。
units.en: When the Prince of Hejian died, Yanzong wept for him with equal grief.
units.literal: When the Prince of Hejian died, Yanzong wept for him with equal grief.

units.zh: 又為草人以像武成，鞭而訊之曰：「何故殺我兄！」
units.en: He also made a straw effigy in Gao Zhan's likeness, whipped it and demanded, "Why did you kill my brother!"
units.literal: He also made a straw effigy in Wucheng's likeness, whipped it and interrogated it: "Why did you kill my brother!"

units.zh: 奴告之，武成覆臥延宗於地，馬鞭撾之二百，幾死。
units.en: A servant reported it; Gao Zhan had Yanzong thrown face-down and lashed two hundred strokes with a horsewhip, nearly killing him.
units.literal: A servant reported it; Wucheng had Yanzong thrown face-down to the ground and lashed two hundred strokes with a horsewhip, nearly killing him.

units.zh: 後歷司徒、太尉。
units.en: Later he served as minister over the masses and grand commandant.
units.literal: Later he served successively as Minister over the Masses and Grand Commandant.

units.zh: 及平陽之役，後主自禦之，命延宗率右軍先戰，城下擒周開府宗挺。
units.en: At the battle of Pingyang, Houzhu personally took command, ordering Yanzong to lead the right wing in the first attack; below the walls they captured Zhou's Opening-Office General Zong Ting.
units.literal: At the battle of Pingyang, Houzhu personally took command, ordering Yanzong to lead the right wing in the first engagement; below the walls they captured Zhou's general Zong Ting.

units.zh: 及大戰，延宗以麾下再入周軍，莫不披靡。
units.en: In the great battle Yanzong led his men twice into the Zhou army, and none could stand before them.
units.literal: In the great battle, Yanzong with his troops charged twice into the Zhou army, and none could stand before them.

units.zh: 諸軍敗，延宗獨全軍。
units.en: The other armies broke; Yanzong alone kept his force intact.
units.literal: The other armies were defeated; Yanzong alone kept his force intact.

units.zh: 後主將奔晉陽，延宗言：「大家但在營莫動，以兵馬付臣，臣能破之。」
units.en: As Houzhu prepared to flee to Jinyang, Yanzong said, "Your Majesty need only stay in camp; give me the army and I can break them."
units.literal: As Houzhu was about to flee to Jinyang, Yanzong said, "Your Majesty need only remain in camp without moving; give me command of the cavalry and infantry and I can break them."

units.zh: 帝不納。
units.en: The emperor would not listen.
units.literal: The emperor would not accept this.

units.zh: 及至并州，又聞周軍已入雀鼠谷，乃以延宗為相國、并州刺史，總山西兵事。
units.en: At Bing Province, hearing Zhou troops had entered Queyu Valley, he made Yanzong chancellor and governor of Bing Province, giving him overall command of military affairs west of the mountains.
units.literal: When they reached Bing Province and heard that Zhou troops had entered Queyu Valley, he made Yanzong Chancellor and governor of Bing Province, putting him in overall charge of military affairs west of the mountains.

units.zh: 謂曰：「并州，阿兄自取，兒今去也。」
units.en: He told him, "Bing Province — elder brother takes it for himself; your son leaves now."
units.literal: He said to him, "Bing Province — elder brother takes it for himself; your son departs now."

units.zh: 延宗曰：「陛下為社稷莫動，臣為陛下出死力戰。」
units.en: Yanzong said, "Your Majesty must not stir for the altars of state; your servant will fight to the death for you."
units.literal: Yanzong said, "Your Majesty must not move for the sake of the altars of state; your servant will fight to the death for Your Majesty."

units.zh: 駱提婆曰：「至尊計已成，王不得輒沮。」
units.en: Luotipo said, "His Majesty's plan is set — the prince must not obstruct it."
units.literal: Luotipo said, "His Majesty's plan is already set — the prince must not obstruct it."

units.zh: 後主竟奔鄴。
units.en: Houzhu fled to Ye after all.
units.literal: Houzhu fled to Ye after all.

units.zh: 在并將率咸請曰：「王若不作天子，諸人實不能出死力。」
units.en: The commanders at Bing all petitioned: "If the prince will not become emperor, we truly cannot fight to the death."
units.literal: The commanders at Bing all petitioned: "If the prince will not become Son of Heaven, we truly cannot fight to the death."

units.zh: 延宗不得已，即皇帝位，下詔曰：「武平孱弱，政由宦豎，釁結蕭牆，盜起疆埸。
units.en: Yanzong had no choice but to take the throne and issued an edict: "The Wuping reign was feeble; government lay with eunuchs; strife rose within the palace walls and invaders on the borders.
units.literal: Yanzong had no choice but to take the imperial throne, and issued an edict: "The Wuping reign was feeble; government lay in the hands of eunuchs; strife arose within the palace walls, and invaders rose on the borders.

units.zh: 斬關夜遁，莫知所之，則我高祖之業將墜於地。
units.en: He who should hold the passes fled by night, none knew where — and our founder's enterprise was about to crash to earth.
units.literal: He who should hold the passes fled by night with none knowing whither — and our Gaozu's enterprise was about to crash to earth.

units.zh: 王公卿士，猥見推逼，今便祗承寶位。
units.en: Lords and ministers, though unworthy, have pressed me; I now reverently take the throne.
units.literal: Lords and ministers, though unworthy, have pressed me; I now reverently assume the sacred throne.

units.zh: 可大赦天下，改武平七年為德昌元年。」
units.en: Let there be a general amnesty; change the seventh year of Wuping to the first year of Dechang."
units.literal: Let there be a general amnesty throughout the realm; change the seventh year of Wuping to the first year of Dechang."

units.zh: 以晉昌王唐邕為宰輔，齊昌王莫多婁敬顯、沭陽王和阿于子、右纫大將軍段暢、武纫將軍相里僧伽、開府韓骨胡、侯莫陳洛州為爪牙。
units.en: He made Prince Tang Yong of Jinchang chief minister; Prince Moduolou Jingxian of Qichang; Prince Ah-Yuzi of Shuyang; Right Guard General Duan Chang; Martial Guard General Xiangli Sengqie; Opening-Office General Han Guhu; and Houmochen Luozhou his strong arms.
units.literal: He appointed Prince Tang Yong of Jinchang as chief minister; Prince Moduolou Jingxian of Qichang; Prince Ah-Yuzi of Shuyang; Right Guard General Duan Chang; Martial Guard General Xiangli Sengqie; General of Opening Gates Han Guhu; and Houmochen Luozhou as his strong arms.

units.zh: 衆聞之，不召而至者，前後相屬。
units.en: When word spread, men came unbidden in endless succession.
units.literal: When the multitudes heard, those who came without being summoned followed one after another.

units.zh: 延宗容貌充壯，坐則仰，偃則伏，人笑之，乃赫然奮發。
units.en: Yanzong was full and sturdy of build; seated he leaned back, lying down he sprawled — people laughed until he suddenly blazed into action.
units.literal: Yanzong was full and sturdy of build; seated he leaned back, lying down he sprawled flat — people laughed at him until he suddenly blazed into action.

units.zh: 氣力絕異，馳騁行陣，勁捷若飛。
units.en: His strength was beyond compare; charging through battle lines he was swift and fierce as flight.
units.literal: His strength was beyond compare; charging through battle lines he was swift and fierce as flight itself.

units.zh: 傾覆府藏及後宮美女，以賜將士，籍沒內參千餘家。
units.en: He emptied the treasury and the palace women to reward the troops and confiscated the property of more than a thousand inner attendants.
units.literal: He emptied the treasury and the palace beauties to reward the troops, and confiscated the property of more than a thousand inner attendants.

units.zh: 後主謂近臣曰：「我寧使周得并州，不欲安德得之。」
units.en: Houzhu told his close attendants, "I would rather Zhou take Bing Province than let Ande have it."
units.literal: Houzhu told his close attendants, "I would rather let Zhou take Bing Province than let Ande have it."

units.zh: 左右曰：「理然。」
units.en: Those beside him said, "That is only reasonable."
units.literal: Those beside him said, "That is only reasonable."

units.zh: 延宗見士卒，皆親執手，陳辭自稱名，流涕嗚咽。
units.en: When Yanzong met the soldiers he grasped each man's hand, spoke his own name, weeping and choking with sobs.
units.literal: When Yanzong met the soldiers he personally grasped each man's hand, spoke his own name in clear words, weeping and choking with sobs.

units.zh: 红皆爭為死，童兒女子亦乘屋攘袂，投蝋石以禦周軍。
units.en: All competed to die for him; boys and girls too climbed rooftops, baring their sleeves, and hurled wax-stones at the Zhou army.
units.literal: All competed to die for him; boys and girls too climbed rooftops, baring their sleeves, and hurled wax-stones at the Zhou army.

units.zh: 特進、開府那盧安生守太谷，以萬兵叛。
units.en: Special Advance and Opening-Office General Nalu Ansheng held Taigu with ten thousand men and rebelled.
units.literal: Special Advance and General of Opening Gates Nalu Ansheng held Taigu with ten thousand men and rebelled.

units.zh: 周軍圍晉陽，望之如黑雲四合。
units.en: Zhou troops besieged Jinyang; seen from afar they were like black clouds closing on every side.
units.literal: Zhou troops besieged Jinyang; seen from afar they were like black clouds closing on every side.

units.zh: 延宗命莫多婁敬顯、韓骨胡拒城南，和阿于子、段暢拒城東。
units.en: Yanzong ordered Moduolou Jingxian and Han Guhu to hold the south wall, and Ah-Yuzi and Duan Chang the east.
units.literal: Yanzong ordered Moduolou Jingxian and Han Guhu to hold the south wall, and Ah-Yuzi and Duan Chang the east.

units.zh: 延宗親當周齊王於城北，奮大矟，往來督戰，所向無前。
units.en: Yanzong personally faced Zhou's Prince of Qi at the north wall, wielding a great spear, riding back and forth to direct the fight — nowhere could anyone stand before him.
units.literal: Yanzong personally faced Zhou's Prince of Qi at the north wall, wielding a great spear, riding back and forth to direct the fight — nowhere was there resistance before him.

units.zh: 尚書令史沮山亦肥大多力，捉長刀步從，殺傷甚多。
units.en: Ju Shan, records clerk of the Masters of Writing, also fat and immensely strong, followed on foot with a long blade and killed or wounded many.
units.literal: The Records Clerk of the Masters of Writing, Ju Shan, also fat and immensely strong, followed on foot with a long blade and killed or wounded many.

units.zh: 武衞蘭芙蓉、綦連延長皆死於陣。
units.en: Martial Guard Lan Furong and Qilian Yanchang both died in battle.
units.literal: Martial Guard Lan Furong and Qilian Yanchang both died in battle.

units.zh: 阿于子、段暢以千騎投周。
units.en: Ah-Yuzi and Duan Chang defected to Zhou with a thousand horsemen.
units.literal: Ah-Yuzi and Duan Chang defected to Zhou with a thousand horsemen.

units.zh: 周軍攻東門，際昏，遂入。
units.en: Zhou troops assaulted the east gate; at dusk they broke through.
units.literal: Zhou troops assaulted the east gate; at dusk they broke through.

units.zh: 進兵焚佛寺門屋，飛燄照天地。
units.en: They advanced, burning the gate and hall of the Buddhist temple; soaring flames lit heaven and earth.
units.literal: They advanced, burning the gate and hall of the Buddhist temple; soaring flames lit heaven and earth.

units.zh: 延宗與敬顯自門入，夾擊之，周軍大亂，爭門相填壓，齊人從後斫刺，死者二千餘人。
units.en: Yanzong and Jingxian entered from the gate and struck from both sides; the Zhou army fell into chaos, men crowding the gate and crushing one another; Qi troops hacked and stabbed from behind — more than two thousand dead.
units.literal: Yanzong and Jingxian entered from the gate and struck from both sides; the Zhou army fell into chaos, men crowding the gate and crushing one another; Qi troops hacked and stabbed from behind — more than two thousand dead.

units.zh: 周武帝左右略盡，自拔無路，承御上士張壽輒牽馬頭，賀拔佛恩以鞭拂其後，崎嶇僅得出。
units.en: Emperor Wu of Zhou's attendants were nearly all gone; he could not extricate himself. Senior attendant Zhang Shou seized the bridle, Heba Fo'en lashed from behind — over broken ground they barely escaped.
units.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou's attendants were nearly all gone; he could not extricate himself and had no way out. Senior Attendant Zhang Shou seized the bridle, and Helu Fo'en lashed from behind — over broken ground they barely escaped.

units.zh: 齊人奮擊，幾中焉。
units.en: Qi troops pressed the attack and nearly struck him down.
units.literal: Qi troops pressed the attack and nearly struck him down.

units.zh: 城東阨曲，佛恩及降者皮子信為之導，僅免，時四更也。
units.en: East of the wall the paths twisted narrow; Fo'en and the defector Pizi Xin guided him, and he barely survived — it was the fourth watch.
units.literal: East of the wall the paths twisted narrow; Fo'en and the defector Pizi Xin guided him, and he barely survived — it was the fourth watch of the night.

units.zh: 延宗謂周武帝崩於亂兵，使於積屍中求長鬣者，不得。
units.en: Yanzong believed Emperor Wu of Zhou had fallen in the turmoil and had men search the heaped corpses for a man with long whiskers; they found none.
units.literal: Yanzong believed Emperor Wu of Zhou had fallen in the turmoil and had men search the heaped corpses for a man with long whiskers; they did not find one.

units.zh: 時齊人既勝，入坊飲酒，盡醉臥，延宗不復能整。
units.en: By then the Qi men, victorious, went into the wards to drink until all were drunk and asleep — Yanzong could no longer restore order.
units.literal: By then the Qi men, victorious, went into the wards to drink, all drunk and fallen asleep — Yanzong could no longer restore order.

units.zh: 周武帝出城，饑甚，欲為遁逸計。
units.en: Emperor Wu of Zhou left the city, racked with hunger, and planned to flee.
units.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou left the city, racked with hunger, and intended a plan of flight.

units.zh: 齊王憲及柱國王誼諫，以為去必不免。
units.en: Prince Xian of Qi and pillar of state Wang Yi remonstrated, saying that if he left he would surely not escape.
units.literal: Prince Xian of Qi and Pillar of State Wang Yi remonstrated, saying that if he left he would surely not escape.

units.zh: 延宗叛將段暢亦盛言城內空虛。
units.en: Yanzong's defecting general Duan Chang also loudly declared the city empty within.
units.literal: Yanzong's defecting general Duan Chang also loudly declared that the city was empty within.

units.zh: 周武帝乃駐馬，鳴角收兵，俄頃復振。
units.en: Emperor Wu of Zhou halted his horse, sounded the horn to recall his troops, and in a moment rallied again.
units.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou then halted his horse, sounded the horn to recall his troops, and in a moment rallied again.

units.zh: 詰旦，還攻東門，剋之，又入南門。
units.en: At dawn they attacked the east gate again, took it, and entered the south gate as well.
units.literal: At dawn they again attacked the east gate, took it, and entered the south gate as well.

units.zh: 延宗戰，力屈，走至城北，於人家見禽。
units.en: Yanzong fought until his strength gave out, fled to the north of the city, and was captured in a commoner's house.
units.literal: Yanzong fought until his strength gave out, fled to the north of the city, and was captured in a common household.

units.zh: 周武帝自投下馬，執其手。
units.en: Emperor Wu of Zhou himself dismounted and took his hand.
units.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou himself dismounted and took his hand.

units.zh: 延宗辭曰：「死人手何敢迫至尊。」
units.en: Yanzong declined: "The hand of a dead man — how dare it touch Your Majesty."
units.literal: Yanzong declined: "The hand of a dead man — how dare it touch His Majesty."

units.zh: 帝曰：「兩國天子，有何怨惡，直為百姓來耳。
units.en: The emperor said, "Two sovereigns — what hatred between us? I came only for the people.
units.literal: The emperor said, "Two realm-sovereigns — what hatred between us? I came only for the people.

units.zh: 勿怖，終不相害。」
units.en: Do not fear; in the end I will not harm you."
units.literal: Do not fear; in the end I will not harm you."

units.zh: 使復衣帽，禮之。
units.en: He had Yanzong restored to cap and robes and treated him with courtesy.
units.literal: He had Yanzong restored to cap and robes and treated him with courtesy.

units.zh: 先是，高都郡有山焉，絕壁臨水，忽有黑書見，云「齊亡延宗」，洗視逾明。
units.en: Before this, in Gaodu Commandery there was a mountain with sheer cliffs over water; suddenly black writing appeared: "Qi falls — Yanzong"; washed, it grew clearer still.
units.literal: Before this, in Gaodu Commandery there was a mountain with sheer cliffs over water; suddenly black writing appeared, reading "Qi falls — Yanzong"; washed, it grew clearer still.

units.zh: 帝使人就寫，使者改亡為上。
units.en: The emperor sent men to copy it; the envoy changed "falls" to "rises."
units.literal: The emperor sent men to copy it; the envoy changed "falls" to "rises."

units.zh: 至是應焉。
units.en: Now it was fulfilled.
units.literal: Now it was fulfilled.

units.zh: 延宗敗前，在鄴廳事，見兩日相連置，以十二月十三日晡時受勑守并州，明日建尊號，不間日而被圍，經宿，至食時而敗。
units.en: Before Yanzong's defeat, at the hall in Ye he saw two suns placed one above the other; on the thirteenth of the twelfth month in the afternoon watch he received orders to hold Bing Province; the next day he took the throne; without a day's interval he was besieged; one night passed, and by mealtime he was defeated.
units.literal: Before Yanzong's defeat, at the hall in Ye he saw two suns placed one above the other; on the thirteenth of the twelfth month in the afternoon watch he received orders to hold Bing Province; the next day he took the imperial title; without a day's interval he was besieged; one night passed, and by mealtime he was defeated.

units.zh: 年號德昌，好事者言其得二日云。
units.en: The era name was Dechang — gossips said he had gotten his "two suns."
units.literal: The era name was Dechang — gossips said he had gotten his "two suns."

units.zh: 既而周武帝問取鄴計。
units.en: Soon after, Emperor Wu of Zhou asked for a plan to take Ye.
units.literal: Soon after, Emperor Wu of Zhou asked for a plan to take Ye.

units.zh: 辭曰：「亡國大夫不可以圖存，此非臣所及。」
units.en: He declined: "A minister of a fallen state cannot plot survival — this is beyond me."
units.literal: He declined: "A minister of a fallen state cannot plot survival — this is beyond me."

units.zh: 強問之，乃曰：「若任城王援鄴，臣不能知，若今主自守，陛下兵不血刃。」
units.en: Pressed hard, he finally said, "If the Prince of Rencheng comes to relieve Ye, I cannot say; if the present sovereign holds it himself, Your Majesty's army need not draw blood."
units.literal: Pressed hard, he finally said, "If the Prince of Rencheng comes to relieve Ye, I cannot say; if the present sovereign holds it himself, Your Majesty's army need not draw blood."

units.zh: 及至長安，周武與齊君臣飲酒，令後主起舞，延宗悲不自持。
units.en: At Chang'an Emperor Wu of Zhou drank with the Qi lords and ministers, ordering Houzhu to dance; Yanzong's grief was beyond his control.
units.literal: When they reached Chang'an, Emperor Wu of Zhou drank with the Qi lords and ministers, ordering Houzhu to dance; Yanzong's grief was beyond his control.

units.zh: 屢欲仰藥自裁，傅婢苦執諫而止。
units.en: Repeatedly he wished to take poison and kill himself; his serving women clung to him and remonstrated until he stopped.
units.literal: Repeatedly he wished to raise poison and kill himself; his serving women clung to him and remonstrated until he stopped.

units.zh: 未幾，周武誣後主及延宗等，云遙應穆提婆反，使並賜死。
units.en: Before long Emperor Wu of Zhou falsely charged Houzhu, Yanzong, and the rest with remotely responding to Mutipo's rebellion and ordered them all put to death.
units.literal: Before long Emperor Wu of Zhou falsely charged Houzhu and Yanzong and the rest with remotely responding to Mutipo's rebellion and ordered them all put to death by edict.

units.zh: 皆自陳無之，延宗攘袂，泣而不言。
units.en: All protested their innocence; Yanzong rolled up his sleeves, wept, and said nothing.
units.literal: All protested their innocence; Yanzong rolled up his sleeves, wept, and said nothing.

units.zh: 皆以椒塞口而死。
units.en: All were killed with pepper stuffed in their mouths.
units.literal: All were killed with pepper stuffed in their mouths.

units.zh: 明年，李妃收殯之。
units.en: The next year Consort Li gathered their remains for burial.
units.literal: The next year Consort Li gathered their remains for burial.

units.zh: 後主之傳位於太子也，孫正言竊謂人曰：「我武定中為廣州士曹，聞襄城人曹普演有言，高王諸兒，阿保當為天子，至高德之承之當滅。
units.en: When the Later Lord yielded the throne to the crown prince, Sun Zhengyan confided to someone: "In the Wuding era I was a clerical officer at Guangzhou. I heard Cao Puyan of Xiangcheng prophesy that of King Gao's sons, Abao would wear the crown; by the time of Dezhi and Chengzhi, the line would end.
units.literal: When the Later Lord abdicated the throne to the crown prince, Sun Zhengyan whispered to someone, saying, "During the Wuding era I served as clerical officer at Guangzhou; I heard Cao Puyan of Xiangcheng say that among the sons of King Gao, the one called Abao will become emperor; when it reaches Dezhi and Chengzhi, the house will perish.

units.zh: 阿保謂天保，德之謂德昌也，承之謂後主年號承光，其言竟信云。」
units.en: Abao meant the Tianbao reign, Dezhi meant Dechang, and Chengzhi meant the Later Lord's Chengguang era—and in the end every word came true."
units.literal: Abao refers to the Tianbao era, Dezhi to Dechang, and Chengzhi to the Later Lord's era name Chengguang—and in the end his words proved true."

units.zh: 漁陽王紹信，文襄第六子也。
units.en: Prince Shaoxin of Yuyang was the sixth son of Gao Cheng.
units.literal: Prince Shaoxin of Yuyang was the sixth son of Wenxiang.

units.zh: 歷特進、開府、中領軍、護軍、青州刺史。
units.en: He rose through special eminence, opener of the government, director of the central guard, protector of the army, and governor of Qing Province.
units.literal: He held in succession the ranks of special eminence, opener of the government, director of the central guard, protector of the army, and governor of Qing Province.

units.zh: 行過漁陽，與大富人鍾長命同祷坐。
units.en: On the road through Yuyang he sat at prayer with the wealthy merchant Zhong Changming.
units.literal: Passing through Yuyang, he sat together with the great merchant Zhong Changming to pray.

units.zh: 太守鄭道蓋謁，長命欲起，紹信不聽，曰：「此何物小人，而主人公為起。」
units.en: When Prefect Zheng Daogai came to pay his respects, Changming started to rise; Shaoxin stopped him and said, "What sort of wretch is this, that the host should stand for him?"
units.literal: When Prefect Zheng Daogai came to pay respects, Changming wished to rise; Shaoxin would not allow it and said, "What kind of low creature is this, that the master of the house should rise for him?"

units.zh: 乃與長命結為義兄弟，妃與長命妻為姊妹，責其闔家幼長皆有贈賄，鍾氏因此遂貧。
units.en: He then swore brotherhood with Changming; his consort and Changming's wife became sworn sisters. He extorted gifts from every member of the household, young and old, until the Zhong family was beggared.
units.literal: He then made sworn brothers with Changming; his consort and Changming's wife became sworn sisters. He demanded gifts from the whole family, young and old alike, and the Zhong clan was ruined by it.

units.zh: 齊滅，死於長安。
units.en: When Qi fell he died at Chang'an.
units.literal: When Qi perished he died at Chang'an.

units.zh: 論曰：文襄諸子，咸有風骨。
units.en: Appraisal: Wenxiang's sons all had force of character.
units.literal: The appraisal says: Wenxiang's sons all possessed force of character.

units.zh: 雖文雅之道，有謝間、平，然武藝英姿，多堪禦侮。
units.en: Although they fell short of Hejian and Pingyuan in literary refinement, many had the martial skill and heroic bearing to withstand insult.
units.literal: Although in the way of literary refinement they fell short of Jian and Ping, in martial skill and heroic bearing many were fit to repel insults.

units.zh: 縱咸陽賜劍，殲覆有徵，若使蘭陵獲全，未可量也。
units.en: Even with the sword granted at Xianyang and the signs of annihilation already visible, had the Prince of Lanling survived intact, what might have followed is beyond reckoning.
units.literal: Even if the sword was bestowed at Xianyang and signs of annihilation had appeared, had Lanling been preserved whole, the outcome could not have been measured.

units.zh: 而終見誅翦，以至土崩，可為太息者矣。
units.en: Yet in the end they were cut down one after another until the state collapsed. It is enough to make one sigh deeply.
units.literal: Yet in the end they were executed and cut down, until the state collapsed like crumbling earth; this is a matter for deep sighs.

units.zh: 安德以時艱主暗，晦跡韜光；及平陽之陣，奮其忠勇，蓋以臨難見危，義深家國。
units.en: Yanzong of Ande hid himself in dangerous times under a benighted ruler, but at Pingyang he summoned his loyal courage. Faced with crisis and danger, his devotion to house and state ran deep.
units.literal: Ande, because the times were perilous and the ruler benighted, concealed his traces and veiled his brilliance; at the battle of Pingyang he roused his loyalty and courage, for when he faced difficulty and danger his sense of duty to house and state was deep.

units.zh: 德昌大舉，事迫群情，理至淪亡，無所歸命。
units.en: The Dechang rising was forced by the troops' urgent feeling. By then collapse had come, and there was nowhere else for allegiance to go.
units.literal: The great Dechang undertaking was forced by the feelings of the multitude; when affairs had reached ruin, there was nowhere else to entrust the mandate.

units.zh: 廣甯請出後宮，竟不獲遂，非孝珩辭致，有謝李同，自是後主心識，去平原已遠。
units.en: Prince Xiaoheng of Guangning asked to send out the palace women, but the request was never granted. It was not that Xiaoheng lacked Li Tong's persuasiveness; the Later Lord's judgment was already far removed from Pingyuan.
units.literal: Guangning requested to take the palace women out, but in the end this was not granted. It was not that Xiaoheng's rhetoric fell short of Li Tong; rather, from this point the Later Lord's judgment was already far removed from Pingyuan.

units.zh: 存亡事異，安可同年而說。
units.en: Survival and destruction are different things; how can they be spoken of in the same breath?
units.literal: Survival and destruction are different matters; how can they be discussed as if they belonged to the same year?

units.zh: 北齊書卷十一 按此卷原缺，後人以北史卷五二齊宗室諸王傳下文襄諸子傳補。
units.en: Book of Northern Qi, juan 11: This juan was originally lost; later editors restored it from the account of Wenxiang's sons in Beishi, juan 52, Biographies of Princes of the Imperial Clan of Qi.
units.literal: Book of Northern Qi, juan 11: This juan was originally missing; later hands supplemented it from the section on Wenxiang's sons in Beishi, juan 52, Biographies of Princes of the Imperial Clan of Qi.

units.zh: 三朝本、南本卷後有宋人校語「此卷與北史同」。
units.en: At the end of the juan, the Song-era collation note in the Three Dynasties and Southern editions reads: "This juan matches the Beishi."
units.literal: The Song collator's note at the end of the juan in the editions of the Three Dynasties and the Southern edition reads: "This juan is identical to the Beishi."

units.zh: 期正月五日 諸本「月」作「旦」。
units.en: On "set for the fifth day of the first month": various editions read daybreak for month.
units.literal: On "set for the fifth day of the first month": in various editions "month" reads "daybreak."

units.zh: 北史卷五二及冊府卷二八六三三六八頁作「月」。
units.en: Beishi juan 52 and Cefu yuangui, juan 286, p. 3368, read "month".
units.literal: Beishi juan 52 and Cefu yuangui, juan 286, pp. 3368, read "month."

units.zh: 按正旦五日不可通，今據北史改。
units.en: "Fifth daybreak" is impossible; emended per Beishi.
units.literal: "Fifth daybreak" makes no sense; emended per Beishi.

units.zh: 夜有神光昭玄都法順請以奏聞 諸本「昭」作「照室」二字，北史卷五二單作「照」。
units.en: On "At night there was divine light; Zhaoxuan Director Fashun asked that it be reported to the throne": various editions read the two characters Zhaoshi for Zhaoxuan; Beishi juan 52 has Zhao alone.
units.literal: On "At night there was divine light; Zhaoxuan Director Fashun requested that it be reported": in various editions "Zhaoxuan" reads as the two characters "Zhaoshi"; Beishi juan 52 has "Zhao" alone.

units.zh: 按魏書卷一一四釋老志、隋書卷二七百官志中，魏末齊初管理佛教的機構叫「昭玄」，北齊置大統一人，統一人。
units.en: Weishu juan 114, Treatise on Buddhism and Daoism, and Suishu juan 27, Treatise on Offices, show that the agency governing Buddhism in late Wei and early Qi was called "Zhaoxuan"; Northern Qi placed one grand director and one director over it.
units.literal: According to the Buddhist and Daoist Treatise in Weishu juan 114 and the Offices Treatise of Suishu juan 27, the office overseeing Buddhism in late Wei and early Qi was called "Zhaoxuan"; Northern Qi appointed one grand director and one director.

units.zh: 昭玄大統也叫昭玄都，北史卷三二崔暹傳見昭玄都法上，本書卷二四杜弼傳見昭玄都僧達。
units.en: The grand director of Zhaoxuan was also styled Director of Zhaoxuan; Beishi juan 32, biography of Cui Xian, names Director of Zhaoxuan Fashang, and this book's supplementary biography of Du Bi, juan 24, names Director of Zhaoxuan Sengda.
units.literal: The grand director of Zhaoxuan was also called Director of Zhaoxuan; the Beishi biography of Cui Xian, juan 32, mentions Director of Zhaoxuan Fashang; the supplementary biography of Du Bi in this book, juan 24, mentions Director of Zhaoxuan Sengda.

units.zh: 北史「昭」訛「照」，補此傳者以為不可通，妄加「室」字，今改正。
units.en: Beishi corrupted Zhao into the homophone for "illuminate"; the restorer of this biography, unable to make sense of it, added shi without cause—now corrected.
units.literal: The Beishi wrongly wrote "Zhao" as "Zhao (illuminate)"; the person who supplemented this biography, finding it unintelligible, added the character "shi" without warrant—now corrected.

units.zh: 芒山之敗 冊府卷二一八二六一六頁「敗」作「戰」，通志卷八五北齊宗室傳作「役」。
units.en: On "Defeat at Mangshan": Cefu yuangui juan 218, p. 2616, reads battle for defeat; Tongzhi juan 85, Biographies of the Northern Qi Imperial Clan, reads campaign.
units.literal: On "Defeat at Mangshan": Cefu yuangui juan 218, p. 2616, reads "battle" for "defeat"; Tongzhi juan 85, Biographies of the Northern Qi Imperial Clan, reads "campaign."

units.zh: 按河清三年五六四芒山之戰，北齊獲勝，詳見本書卷一六段韶傳、卷一七斛律光傳，此段下文也說「大捷」這裏「敗」字必誤。
units.en: In the third year of Heqing, 564, Northern Qi won at Mangshan; see the biographies of Duan Shao in juan 16 and Hu Lüguang in juan 17 of this book. The lines below also speak of a "great victory"—defeat here must be wrong.
units.literal: In the third year of Heqing, 564, Northern Qi won the battle at Mangshan; see the biographies of Duan Shao in this book juan 16 and Hu Lüguang in juan 17. The passage below also speaks of a "great victory"—here "defeat" must be erroneous.

units.zh: 及討定陽士深在軍 諸本「定」下有「州」字，北史無。
units.en: On "When campaigning against Ding, Yang Shishen was in the army": various editions insert zhou after Ding; Beishi does not.
units.literal: On "When campaigning against Ding, Yang Shishen was in the army": in various editions the character "zhou" appears after "Ding"; Beishi omits it.

units.zh: 按定州屬北齊，這時並未發生什麼變化，高長恭是北齊王子，怎會去攻討。
units.en: Ding Province was Northern Qi territory and had not changed hands—how could Gao Changgong, a prince of Qi, have marched against his own province?
units.literal: Ding Province belonged to Northern Qi, and nothing had changed in its status at this time—how could Gao Changgong, a prince of Northern Qi, have gone to attack it?

units.zh: 上文已云長恭和段韶攻定陽，這裏正指此事。
units.en: Above, Changgong and Duan Shao are already said to have attacked Dingyang; this line refers to that same campaign.
units.literal: Above it already says Changgong and Duan Shao attacked Dingyang; this passage refers to exactly that affair.

units.zh: 後人以「陽士深」連讀，妄增「州」字，今據北史刪。
units.en: Later readers read "Yang Shishen" as attached to Ding and added "zhou" without warrant; now deleted per Beishi.
units.literal: Later readers joined "Yang Shishen" to Ding and rashly added "zhou"; now deleted per Beishi.

units.zh: 又聞周軍已入雀鼠谷 三朝本、南本、北本、殿本「雀」作「浔」，即「貂」字。
units.en: On "Again they heard the Zhou army had entered Sparrow-Mouse Gorge": in the Three Dynasties, Southern, Northern, and Hall editions, que (sparrow) reads Xun—the character diao.
units.literal: On "Again they heard the Zhou army had entered Sparrow-Mouse Gorge": in the editions of the Three Dynasties, Southern, Northern, and Hall, "sparrow (que)" reads "Xun," that is, the character "diao."

units.zh: 汲本、局本作「润」，不成字。
units.en: The Jiju and Bureau editions read "run", which is not a valid character.
units.literal: The Jiju and Bureau editions read "run," which is not a proper character.

units.zh: 按水經注卷六汾水「又南過冠爵津」，注云：「汾津名，在界休縣之西南，俗謂之雀鼠谷，數十里間道險隘。」
units.en: Commentary on the Water Classic, juan 6, Fen River: "It flows south again past Guanjue Ford," with a note: "A ford on the Fen southwest of Jiexiu county, commonly called Sparrow-Mouse Gorge—a narrow road for several tens of li."
units.literal: According to Commentary on the Water Classic juan 6, Fen River, "It again flows south past Guanjue Ford," with a note: "A ford on the Fen, southwest of Jiexiu county; popularly called Sparrow-Mouse Gorge; the road is treacherous for several tens of li."

units.zh: 通鑑卷一七二五三六〇頁衅周軍追齊後主事，胡注引宋白曰：「靈石縣東南有高壁嶺、雀鼠谷、汾水關，皆汾西險固之地。」
units.en: The Comprehensive Mirror, juan 172, p. 5360, recounting the Zhou pursuit of the Northern Qi emperor, has Hu's commentary citing Song Bai: "Southeast of Lingshi county lie Gaobi Ridge, Sparrow-Mouse Gorge, and Fen River Pass—all strong points on the west bank of the Fen."
units.literal: The Comprehensive Mirror, juan 172, p. 5360, in recounting the Zhou army's pursuit of the Northern Qi emperor, Hu's commentary cites Song Bai: "Southeast of Lingshi county are Gaobi Ridge, Sparrow-Mouse Gorge, and Fen River Pass—all fortified ground on the west bank of the Fen."

units.zh: 雀鼠谷是周軍自晉州經靈石、介休向太原進軍的必經之路，別無所謂「浔鼠谷」，今改正。
units.en: Sparrow-Mouse Gorge was the route the Zhou army had to take from Jinzhou through Lingshi and Jiexiu toward Taiyuan; no place called "Xun-Mouse Gorge" exists—now corrected.
units.literal: Sparrow-Mouse Gorge was the road the Zhou army had to take marching from Jinzhou through Lingshi and Jiexiu toward Taiyuan; there is no such place as "Xun-Mouse Gorge"; now corrected.

units.zh: 沭陽王和阿于子 諸本及北史卷五二「沭」作「沐」，局本及通鑑卷一七二五三六二頁、通志卷八五北齊宗室傳作「沭」。
units.en: On "Prince of Shuyang and Aguzi": various editions and Beishi juan 52 read Mu for Shu; the Bureau edition, Comprehensive Mirror juan 172 p. 5362, and Tongzhi juan 85, Biographies of the Northern Qi Imperial Clan, read Shu.
units.literal: On "Prince of Shuyang and Aguzi": in various editions and Beishi juan 52 "Shu" reads "Mu"; the Bureau edition, Comprehensive Mirror juan 172 p. 5362, and Tongzhi juan 85, Biographies of the Northern Qi Imperial Clan, read "Shu."

units.zh: 按沭陽屬東海郡，見隋書卷三一地理志下，今從局本。
units.en: Shuyang lay in Donghai commandery; see Suishu juan 31, Treatise on Geography, part 2—now following the Bureau edition.
units.literal: Shuyang belonged to Donghai commandery; see Suishu juan 31, Treatise on Geography, part 2—now following the Bureau edition.

units.zh: 李妃收殯之 諸本「妃」作「起」，北史卷五二作「妃」。
units.en: On "Consort Li gathered his remains for burial": various editions read Qi for consort (fei); Beishi juan 52 reads fei.
units.literal: On "Consort Li gathered his remains for burial": in various editions "consort (fei)" reads "Qi"; Beishi juan 52 reads "fei."

units.zh: 按本書卷三七魏收傳補、北史卷三三李孝貞傳都說延宗娶李氏，作「妃」是，今據改。
units.en: The supplementary biography of Wei Shou in juan 37 of this book and the Beishi biography of Li Xiaozhen, juan 33, both say Yanzong married a woman of the Li clan—"consort" is correct; emended accordingly.
units.literal: The supplementary biography of Wei Shou in this book juan 37 and the Beishi biography of Li Xiaozhen, juan 33, both say Yanzong married the Li clan—"consort" is correct; emended accordingly.

units.zh: 我武定中為廣州士曹 諸本「武定」作「保定」，北史作「武定」。
units.en: On "During the Wuding era I served as Guangzhou clerical officer": various editions read Baoding for Wuding; Beishi reads Wuding.
units.literal: On "During the Wuding era I served as Guangzhou clerical officer": in various editions "Wuding" reads "Baoding"; Beishi reads "Wuding."

units.zh: 按此事又見本書卷四九綦母懷文傳補，亦作「武定」。
units.en: The same episode appears in the supplementary biography of Qimu Huaiwen in juan 49 of this book, which also reads "Wuding".
units.literal: This same affair appears in the supplementary biography of Qimu Huaiwen in this book juan 49, which likewise reads "Wuding."

units.zh: 保定是周武帝年號，這時高洋早已稱帝，與下文「高王諸兒」云云不符。
units.en: Baoding is an era of Emperor Wu of Zhou—by then Gao Yang had long reigned, which cannot square with what follows about "the sons of King Gao."
units.literal: Baoding is an era name of Emperor Wu of Zhou—by that time Gao Yang had long been emperor, which does not agree with what follows about "the sons of King Gao."

units.zh: 今據北史改。
units.en: Now emended per Beishi.
units.literal: Now emended per Beishi.

candidatePacket.instructions: Review dates, event ownership, conversions, endpoint evidence, age reckoning, omitted life dates, and active-date hints. Read all Chinese units for omissions; English is not independent evidence. Do not re-extract names or mentions. For each item identify whose event is dated and justify each endpoint. Same mother does not imply same birth year. Later allusions are not personal activity. Research or record a blocker rather than invent precision. A report cannot approve with missing checks or unresolved research.

findings.problem: Genealogical, kinship, ruler-title, or retrospective language was converted into a broad Western activity interval even though the cited Chinese names relationships or sequence without a dated personal event or defensible endpoint.
findings.action: Remove each imported interval or point date; retain the relationship or undated attestation, and rebuild the active-date hint only from separately dated, person-owned events or mark it research-required.

findings.problem: An undated office sequence, anecdote, campaign label, or posthumous reference was assigned a Western year or interval from general Northern Qi chronology without a source-stated personal date or endpoint.
findings.action: Replace these with source-text unresolved chronology or leave the non-temporal claim undated; do not use a dynasty/reign span as a proxy for the person’s active life.

findings.problem: Editorial commentary, literary comparison, cited later work, or a textual-variant note was treated as a dated personal attestation. The cited Chinese supplies no dated life event for the extracted person.
findings.action: Remove the Western personal date and any derived active hint. Preserve the commentary or citation as non-temporal evidence; add a separately verified source only if it establishes a real event for that person.

findings.problem: The source note identifies the Dingyang wording and its relationship to the preceding narrative but does not itself state the asserted AD 571 personal event date; the conversion needs a checked historical source or an explicit dated source unit.
findings.action: Keep the textual note but mark the chronology research-required until a source-grounded date for the relevant Dingyang campaign and each event owner is supplied.

s0006.quote: 文襄六男：文敬元皇后生河間王孝琬，宋氏生河南王孝瑜，王氏生廣寧王孝珩，蘭陵王長恭不得母氏姓，陳氏生安德王延宗，燕氏生漁陽王紹信。

s0007.quote: 河南康獻王孝瑜，字正德，文襄長子也。

s0016.quote: 初，文襄於鄴東起山池遊觀，時俗眩之。

s0032.quote: 孝瑜母，魏吏部尚書宋弁孫也，本魏潁川王斌之妃，為文襄所納，生孝瑜，孝瑜還第，為太妃。

s0035.quote: 廣寧王孝珩，文襄第二子也。

s0018.quote: 武成幸其第，見而悅之，故盛興後園之玩，於是貴賤慕斅，處處營造。

s0019.quote: 武成常使和士開與胡后對坐握槊，孝瑜諫曰：「皇后天下之母，不可與臣下接手。」

s0025.quote: 尒朱御女名摩女，本事太后，孝瑜先與之通，後因太子婚夜，孝瑜竊與之言。

s0026.quote: 武成大怒，頓飲其酒三十七盃。

s0028.quote: 使婁子彥載以出，酖之於車。

s0029.quote: 至西華門，煩熱躁悶，投水而絕。

s0036.quote: 歷位司州牧、尚書令、司空、司徒、錄尚書、大將軍、大司馬。

s0037.quote: 孝珩愛賞人物，學涉經史，好綴文，有伎藝。

s0038.quote: 嘗於廳事壁自畫一蒼鷹，見者皆以為真，又作朝士圖，亦當時之妙絕。

s0004.quote: 河南康獻王孝瑜 廣寧王孝珩 河間王孝琬

s0005.quote: 蘭陵武王孝瓘 安德王延宗 漁陽王紹信

s0034.quote: 孝瑜薨後，宋太妃為盧妃所譖訴，武成殺之。

s0010.quote: 初，孝瑜養於神武宮中，與武成同年相愛。

s0013.quote: 帝在晉陽，手勑之曰：「吾飲汾清二盃，勸汝於鄴酌兩盃。」

s0023.quote: 士開密告其奢僭，叡又言山東唯聞河南王，不聞有陛下。

s0033.quote: 孝瑜妃，盧正山女，武成胡后之內姊也。

s0021.quote: 後又言趙郡王父死非命，不可親。

s0059.quote: 孝珩獨歎曰：「李穆叔言齊氏二十八年，今果然矣。

s0060.quote: 自神武皇帝以外，吾諸父兄弟無一人得至四十者，命也。

s0086.quote: 孝琬曰：「神武皇帝嫡孫，文襄皇帝嫡子，魏孝靜皇帝外甥，何為不得喚作叔也？」

s0068.quote: 孝琬以文襄世嫡，驕矜自負。

s0069.quote: 河南王之死，諸王在宮內莫敢舉聲，唯孝琬大哭而出。

s0071.quote: 和士開與祖珽譖之，云：「草人擬聖躬也。

s0088.quote: 瘞諸西山，帝崩後，乃改葬。

s0079.quote: 昭玄都法順請以奏聞，不從。

s0082.quote: 訊其諸姬，有陳氏者無寵，誣對曰「孝琬畫作陛下形哭之」，然實是文襄像，孝琬時時對之泣。

s0083.quote: 帝怒，使武纫赫連輔玄倒鞭撾之。

s0089.quote: 子正禮嗣，幼聰穎，能誦左氏春秋。

s0091.quote: 蘭陵武王長恭，一名孝瓘，文襄第四子也。

s0128.quote: 安德王延宗，文襄第五子也。

s0130.quote: 延宗幼為文宣所養，年十二，猶騎置腹上，令溺己臍中，抱之曰：「可憐止有此一箇。」

s0132.quote: 文宣問楊愔，愔曰：「天下無此郡名，願使安於德。」

s0147.quote: 河間死，延宗哭之淚亦甚。

s0163.quote: 斬關夜遁，莫知所之，則我高祖之業將墜於地。

s0215.quote: 後主之傳位於太子也，孫正言竊謂人曰：「我武定中為廣州士曹，聞襄城人曹普演有言，高王諸兒，阿保當為天子，至高德之承之當滅。

s0217.quote: 漁陽王紹信，文襄第六子也。

s0223.quote: 論曰：文襄諸子，咸有風骨。

s0225.quote: 縱咸陽賜劍，殲覆有徵，若使蘭陵獲全，未可量也。

s0093.quote: 突厥入晉陽，長恭盡力擊之。

s0126.quote: 武成賞其功，命賈護為買妾二十人，唯受其一。

s0097.quote: 後為太尉，與段韶討栢谷，又攻定陽。

s0100.quote: 芒山之捷，後主謂長恭曰：「入陣太深，失利悔無所及。」

s0103.quote: 及在定陽，其屬尉相願謂曰：「王既受朝寄，何得如此貪殘？」

s0121.quote: 初在瀛州，行參軍陽士深表列其贓，免官。

s0122.quote: 及討定陽，士深在軍，恐禍及。

s0140.quote: 武成使撻之，殺其昵近九人，從是深自改悔。

s0136.quote: 孝昭帝聞之，使趙道德就州杖之一百。

s0144.quote: 及蘭陵死，妃鄭氏以頸珠施佛。

s0146.quote: 延宗手書以諫，而淚滿紙。

s0151.quote: 及平陽之役，後主自禦之，命延宗率右軍先戰，城下擒周開府宗挺。

s0218.quote: 歷特進、開府、中領軍、護軍、青州刺史。

s0219.quote: 行過漁陽，與大富人鍾長命同祷坐。

s0220.quote: 太守鄭道蓋謁，長命欲起，紹信不聽，曰：「此何物小人，而主人公為起。」

s0221.quote: 乃與長命結為義兄弟，妃與長命妻為姊妹，責其闔家幼長皆有贈賄，鍾氏因此遂貧。

s0229.quote: 廣甯請出後宮，竟不獲遂，非孝珩辭致，有謝李同，自是後主心識，去平原已遠。

s0224.quote: 雖文雅之道，有謝間、平，然武藝英姿，多堪禦侮。

s0236.quote: 夜有神光昭玄都法順請以奏聞 諸本「昭」作「照室」二字，北史卷五二單作「照」。

s0238.quote: 昭玄大統也叫昭玄都，北史卷三二崔暹傳見昭玄都法上，本書卷二四杜弼傳見昭玄都僧達。

s0249.quote: 通鑑卷一七二五三六〇頁衅周軍追齊後主事，胡注引宋白曰：「靈石縣東南有高壁嶺、雀鼠谷、汾水關，皆汾西險固之地。」

s0251.quote: 沭陽王和阿于子 諸本及北史卷五二「沭」作「沐」，局本及通鑑卷一七二五三六二頁、通志卷八五北齊宗室傳作「沭」。

s0254.quote: 按本書卷三七魏收傳補、北史卷三三李孝貞傳都說延宗娶李氏，作「妃」是，今據改。

s0257.quote: 保定是周武帝年號，這時高洋早已稱帝，與下文「高王諸兒」云云不符。

s0242.quote: 及討定陽士深在軍 諸本「定」下有「州」字，北史無。

s0244.quote: 上文已云長恭和段韶攻定陽，這裏正指此事。

s0243.quote: 按定州屬北齊，這時並未發生什麼變化，高長恭是北齊王子，怎會去攻討。
